newsitem.title: INDIA: Pakistan price rise may boost Indian rice exports.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan price rise may boost Indian rice exports.

text.p: Export demand for India's flavoured, fine grade basmati rice is expected to pick up following a rise in the price of Pakistani basmati last week, traders and analysts said on Friday.

"We are expecting basmati rice exports to pick up as Pakistan's basmati prices have gone up by nearly $15 per tonne during the past week," said Prem Garg, managing director of Sri Lal Mahal Overseas Ltd, a leading Delhi foodgrains exporter.
"Buyers would therefore look for Indian basmati," Garg said.
India and Pakistan are the two major producers and exporters of basmati rice.
Traders said good export demand for Indian basmati had pushed up their export prices to $900 per tonne from $750 per tonne at the same period last year.
"We have already traded nearly 100,000 tonnes of basmati from the kharif crop and we are expecting contracts to rise," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
India harvests two rice crops, with the bulk of the output from the winter crop. Sowing for the winter crop begins in July and the harvest starts from October.
The agriculture ministry expects winter output to be around 71.27 million tonnes.
Export demand for Indian non-basmati rice is expected to pick up moderately from December when Vietnam's rice stocks will have been consumed.
"Probably buyers will turn to India after Vietnam's crop is over," the analyst said.
"We can expect around 500,000 tonne of rice exports during December, January and February," he said.
Traders said Indian semi-hard five percent broken non-basmati rice was quoted at $300 per tonne fob, 10 percent at $285-290, 15 percent at $260 and 25 percent at $240 per tonne.
"We are shipping small, small (rice) cargoes to Russian and African destinations," said an official in another leading Delhi foodgrains export firm.
